pipeline.title: MAC Enrichment
pipeline.description: Normalize per-source MAC fields (cp_new_client_mac, aruba_client_mac, ...) into a unified `client_mac`, then resolve to a DHCP hostname via the infoblox-nios-mac lookup table. Mirrors the IPAM-enrichment pattern but for MAC addresses.

rules.title: mac normalize client_mac from cp_new_client_mac
rules.description: Cradlepoint client-connect events expose the MAC as cp_new_client_mac. Promote it to the unified client_mac field.
rules.source:
rule "mac normalize client_mac from cp_new_client_mac"
when
  has_field("cp_new_client_mac") &&
  !has_field("client_mac")
then
  set_field("client_mac", to_string($message.cp_new_client_mac));
end

rules.title: mac normalize client_mac from aruba_client_mac
rules.description: Aruba AP station events expose the MAC as aruba_client_mac. Promote to client_mac.
rules.source:
rule "mac normalize client_mac from aruba_client_mac"
when
  has_field("aruba_client_mac") &&
  !has_field("client_mac")
then
  set_field("client_mac", to_string($message.aruba_client_mac));
end

rules.title: mac normalize client_mac from dns_client_ip
rules.description: dnstap events carry dns_client_ip but no MAC. Look up the MAC via the infoblox-nios-ip-to-mac table (NIOS host ipv4addrs + fixedaddress) and set client_mac so the downstream `mac enrich client_mac` rule resolves the DHCP hostname. Keying off dns_client_ip (not the Enrichment-pipeline-derived client_ip) so this rule doesn't depend on Enrichment having run first — Graylog runs multiple stream-connected pipelines in parallel, no ordering guarantee. Lookup table's default_single_value is null, so to_string returns empty when there's no NIOS record; mac enrich filters those out.

rules.title: mac enrich client_mac
rules.description: Resolve client_mac to its DHCP-assigned hostname via the infoblox-nios-mac lookup table (CSV synced hourly from NIOS fixedaddrs+leases by /usr/local/sbin/nios_mac_to_graylog_csv.py). Skip when client_mac is empty (set by the IP normalizer for IPs NIOS doesn't know).
